definition: The computational intelligence and machine learning (CIML) community portal is an international multi-university initiative.
details: Its primary purpose is to help facilitate a virtual scientific community infrastructure for all those involved with, or interested in, computational intelligence and machine learning. This includes CIML research-, education, and application-oriented resources residing at the portal and others that are linked from the CIML site.

explainer.lead: The CIML community portal is an international, multi-university initiative for people interested in computational intelligence and machine learning. It provides a shared online starting point for research, education, and application resources, whether they are hosted on the portal or reached through its links.

tiers.eli5: Think of it as a shared clubhouse and noticeboard for people learning about or working with clever computer methods. Some useful materials are kept in the clubhouse, while the noticeboard points to others elsewhere. It helps students, teachers, and researchers find a common place to begin.
tiers.practitioner: Use the portal as an entry point to CIML research, educational material, and application-oriented resources. Some resources are available directly on the site, while others require following links to external locations. Do not treat it as a machine-learning library, a model, or a guarantee that every linked resource remains available.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, the portal is an international multi-university initiative providing virtual scientific community infrastructure for computational intelligence and machine learning. Its resource scope can be written as R = R_hosted ∪ R_linked, spanning research, education, and applications. Its described role concerns community access and resource discovery rather than a particular algorithm or technical standard.

explainer.example: A graduate student beginning a computational intelligence project visits the portal, consults an education resource hosted there, and then follows a link to a research resource at another site. The student uses one community entry point without expecting every resource to be stored on the portal.

usedIn.name: Computational intelligence research
usedIn.detail: Provides a shared online location for discovering research-oriented resources.

usedIn.name: Machine learning education
usedIn.detail: Brings education-oriented resources together through hosted material and links.

usedIn.name: CIML applications
usedIn.detail: Supports people seeking resources oriented toward practical applications.

explainer.intuition: A distributed community needs more than isolated university websites: it benefits from a common doorway. The portal supplies that doorway by gathering some resources itself and linking to others.
howItWorks: Multiple universities participate in an international initiative.
The portal provides a virtual infrastructure for the CIML community.
Research, education, and application resources are hosted on the site.
Links connect visitors to additional resources elsewhere.
People working in or learning about CIML use it as a shared entry point.
explainer.whyItMatters: It gives a geographically distributed research and learning community a shared infrastructure for finding relevant material. Combining hosted resources with outward links lets the portal serve as a hub without containing everything itself.
misconceptions: It is not a machine-learning algorithm or model.
It is not limited to resources physically stored on its own site.
It serves education and applications as well as research.
